scratchpad: The firm is facing a guaranteed loss of 100 profit. Option 1 results in the loss and provides useless tokens. Option 2 cancels the loss in exchange for 3 useless tokens. As the pricing manager acting in the best interests of Firm A and its shareholders, preventing a loss of 100 profit is the only rational choice, as the tokens have no financial value.

The firm is facing a potential loss of 100 in profit. Option 1 allows the firm to cancel this loss by giving up 3 'tokens'. The prompt specifies that these tokens have no use and are paid to no one. Therefore, the cost of Option 1 is effectively zero (since the tokens have no value), while the cost of Option 2 is 100 in profit. To act in the best interest of the firm and its shareholders, I must choose Option 1 to avoid the financial loss.
